frames.table: z = 0 is the measured table surface; origin on the table below the robot base origin; x is the base x axis projected onto the table. This frame is the MuJoCo world of the mirror.
frames.base: robot base frame of the hand-eye extrinsic
frames.object: axis-aligned box, origin at its geometric centre, which is the origin of the mirroring MuJoCo free-joint body
frames.convention: T_a_b maps coordinates in b to a; T_table_object = T_table_camera x T_camera_object
frames.units: metres, radians; quaternions are [w, x, y, z] (MuJoCo order)

calibration.distortion: removed: frames are undistorted into K_new before use

table_plane.equation: normal . p = offset  (p in base coordinates, metres)

usable_for_motion_reasons: no supervised motion check has passed for this extrinsic yet
calibration.motion_note: this mapping reads the camera only. usable_for_motion describes the calibration, and is not made true by a good looking overlay

camera.axes: rotation maps OpenGL camera axes into the table frame, the convention nexus_vision.perception uses

catalogue.note: Session catalogue for the offline real-image run on calib/c920-point-check-02 frames (captured 2026-09-18, camera confirmed in place at the time). The 30.5 mm edge is NOT a calliper measurement: it is what `run_realsim.sh measure` fits from six archived frames (30.2, 30.5, 30.2, 30.5, 31.3, 31.4 mm) and from one live 2026-09-21 frame (30.9 mm). The nominal 25 mm in realsim/config/blocks.json comes from the grasp log and is contradicted by every one of those frames. Measure the block before relying on either number.

tolerances.note: same reasoning as the default catalogue, scaled to a 30.5 mm block

pose.yaw_note: folded into [0, symmetry_step); the block model cannot distinguish poses a whole step apart

pose_filtered.yaw_note: folded into [0, symmetry_step); the block model cannot distinguish poses a whole step apart

filter.note: pose is the raw single-frame fit; pose_filtered is smoothed. Both are logged so the filter can be undone

pose_base.note: the same pose expressed in the robot base frame via T_base_table; the yaw is about the table normal, not the base z axis

assumed.roll_pitch: zero: the block is assumed to lie flat on the plane
assumed.centre_height_origin: support plane + half the known block height; a consequence of known geometry, not a depth measurement

reasons: no part of this colour region meets the assumed plane; it is not where a block resting on it would appear

note: positions and yaw are camera measurements under the stated plane assumption; centre height, roll and pitch are consequences of the measured table and the catalogue block size, not observations

timing.note: time from frame in hand to record built; it excludes capture and disk
